channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks Pakistan's Help Amid Depleting Air Defense Missiles Against Houthi Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia has requested military assistance from Pakistan to defend against Houthi attacks, as the Kingdom's air defense missile supplies are reportedly running low. The United States is not providing the requested military aid to the Saudi prince. This situation highlights the kingdom's vulnerability in its ongoing conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host 2027 CIS Summit in Bukhara; Strengthens International Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the 2027 CIS Summit in Bukhara, with Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan as co-chairs, according to the CIS Secretary General. Foreign media, including TASS and Trend, highlight Uzbekistan's expanding international cooperation, economic development, and cultural heritage. The country also discussed 46 joint projects with the UK.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accelerates AI Integration into State Policy and Economy by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan has made digitalization a key state policy, integrating AI into strategies and services. The 'Digital Uzbekistan-2030' program and 'IT Park' initiatives have boosted the sector. State sources report Uzbekistan leads Central Asia in AI readiness, aiming to become a major AI user country by 2030.

item.title: Affluent Kazakh Families Voluntarily Renounce Social Payments Amid Means-Testing Introduction
item.description: Following news that some state benefits in Kazakhstan will now be means-tested, affluent families have begun voluntarily refusing social payments. Social media shows citizens stating they can support their families independently and believe support should prioritize those in genuine need. Entrepreneurs and fathers like Asen Zhaksylykov and Nurlan Minaydarov have publicly renounced benefits, emphasizing self-reliance and contributing to Kazakhstan's future.

item.title: Uzbekistan Deputy Addresses Citizen Complaints, Initiates Road Repairs in Nukus
item.description: Olga Niyazova, a deputy of the Jokargy Kenes of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, responded to constituent complaints regarding road conditions in Nukus. Following a deputy's inquiry to the Main Directorate of Automobile Roads, asphalt paving work has commenced on the affected streets. This action highlights the significance of deputy inquiries in resolving citizen issues and ensuring accountability from responsible authorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Significant Reduction in Crimes Against Children and by Minors
item.description: Kazakhstan has seen a 45% decrease in particularly grave crimes against children and a 10% reduction in sexual offenses against minors, according to Vice President Yerlan Karin. Crimes committed by minors also dropped by 10%. These improvements are attributed to legislative measures, including the 2024 law on women's rights and child safety, aimed at protecting children and enhancing education and healthcare.

item.title: Foreign National Sentenced for Illegally Crossing Kazakhstan's Border
item.description: A foreign national who illegally crossed Kazakhstan's border after deserting his military service in Russia has been sentenced. The court ordered his deportation and a five-year ban from entering Kazakhstan. He was found guilty of illegally crossing the state border without passing through border control.

item.title: Pakistan Claims Over 20,000 Terrorists, Including TTP Members, Sheltering in Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's Information Minister stated that over 20,000 terrorists, including 6,000 TTP members, are harbored in Afghanistan. He alleged these individuals receive training in safe havens on Afghan territory and urged the Taliban to prevent terrorist activities, a claim denied by Taliban officials.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens in Saudi Arabia Advised on Safety Measures Amidst Attacks
item.description: Kazakh citizens in Saudi Arabia are advised to avoid airports unless necessary and postpone non-urgent travel due to attacks on civilian infrastructure. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urges adherence to local authorities' instructions, avoidance of crowds, and monitoring official communications.

item.title: Serious Crimes Against Children Decreased by 45%, Reports Yerlan Karin
item.description: The number of particularly serious crimes against children in Kazakhstan has decreased by 45%, according to Vice President Yerlan Karin. He chaired a meeting on implementing presidential initiatives for child welfare, including the "Children of Kazakhstan" concept for 2026-2030. Over $2.5 billion has been allocated to over 7 million children via the "National Fund for Children" program.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region. Previously, he served as the head of the Department for Public Security and Rule of Law within the Presidential Administration. This appointment follows the previous governor's transition to a new role as First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Baxtiyorovich Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region, as announced by presidential press secretary Sherzod Asadov. Qodirov previously headed the Presidential Administration's Department for Public Security and Rule of Law since July 2025. Before that, he served as an advisor on coordinating law enforcement activities.

item.title: Kazakhstan advises citizens in Saudi Arabia to avoid travel due to increased attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs recommends citizens in Saudi Arabia exercise increased caution and avoid non-urgent travel. This advice follows recent attacks on civilian infrastructure. Citizens are urged to follow local authorities' instructions and avoid crowded places and high-risk areas. Contact information for the embassy and consulates is provided.

item.title: Kazakh MFA advises citizens in Saudi Arabia to exercise caution due to attacks
item.description: Due to attacks on Saudi Arabia's civilian infrastructure, Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs recommends its citizens in the country to observe increased security measures. The ministry advises citizens to follow local authorities' instructions and avoid places with mass gatherings and high-risk objects.

item.title: Botir Kudratkhodjayev Appointed New Defense Minister of Uzbekistan
item.description: Botir Kudratkhodjayev has been appointed as the new Defense Minister of Uzbekistan by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Kudratkhodjayev, a Major General, previously served as the First Deputy Interior Minister. He also led the Ministry of Emergency Situations and held various prosecutor positions before his current appointment, replacing Lieutenant General Shuhrat Kholmukhamedov.

item.title: Kazakhstan's MFA Advises Citizens on Safety Amid Saudi Arabia Attacks
item.description: Following attacks on civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has urged Kazakh citizens in the country to exercise heightened caution and follow local authorities' directives. Citizens are advised to avoid non-essential travel, especially to airports, and to stay clear of crowded places and potentially dangerous sites.

item.title: Kazakh President and Belgian Royal Couple Visit Children's Rehabilitation Center in Astana
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, King Philippe, and Queen Mathilde of Belgium visited the National Center for Children's Rehabilitation in Astana. The center provides annual assistance to over 5,000 patients from across Kazakhstan, utilizing medical, psycho-pedagogical, and social adaptation methods, including robotic rehabilitation technologies.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Sentenced to 16 Years in Georgia for Strong Painkiller; MFA Monitoring
item.description: Kazakhstan's Embassy in Georgia is monitoring the case of a Kazakh truck driver sentenced to 16 years for possessing a potent painkiller. Consular staff have visited the citizen, attended court hearings, and assisted in finding legal representation. The man was detained in April with the medication, which is controlled in Georgia, despite having a prescription from Germany.

item.title: Kazakh Company Fined 393 Million Tenge for Illegal Hazardous Waste Processing
item.description: A company in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, has been fined 393 million tenge for illegally processing over 1,400 tons of hazardous oil waste without a license. The director received a two-year, six-month suspended sentence and property confiscation. The illegal profits were seized for the state. This follows previous incidents of illegal waste disposal in the Zhambyl region.

item.title: Kremlin Rejects Ukraine's 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal for Elections
item.description: The Kremlin has rejected Ukraine's proposal for a 60-day ceasefire to hold presidential elections, stating it would allow Ukraine to regroup for further conflict. Russia might consider a one-day pause only on the election day itself, if elections are scheduled. Ukraine previously suggested this for campaign and voting conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Residents Complain About InDrive Drivers Overcharging During Yandex Outage
item.description: Kazakhstan residents have complained about InDrive drivers significantly increasing fares during a recent outage of the Yandex ride-hailing service. Passengers reported that drivers were charging up to double the usual price. Many users expressed frustration on social media, questioning the lack of fare caps on the InDrive platform.

item.title: Almaty Aims to Transform Tourism Model with New "Almaty SuperSki" Project
item.description: The "Almaty SuperSki" project aims to develop Almaty's mountain cluster into a year-round tourist destination, not just a seasonal ski resort. The plan includes building approximately 60 kilometers of ski slopes, with 70% designated for children and beginners. This initiative seeks to attract families and novice skiers, diversifying the region's tourism offerings.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Leaders Discuss Strategic Partnership via Phone Call
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a phone conversation with Turkmenistan's Gurbanguli Berdimuhamedov. During the call, both leaders positively noted the consistently developing and practically enriching strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. The discussion focused on strengthening bilateral ties and cooperation.

item.title: Twelve Local Officials Penalized for Illegal Landfills in East Kazakhstan Region
item.description: In the East Kazakhstan region, twelve rural district administrators (akim) have been brought to administrative responsibility due to illegal landfills. The violations were discovered during an inspection as part of the "Clean Kazakhstan" environmental campaign. Prosecutors identified fifteen unauthorized dumpsites after reviewing satellite imagery and inspecting the territory.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Legal Protections for Human Trafficking Victims
item.description: Kazakhstan has enhanced its legal framework to combat human trafficking and protect victims, according to MP Marat Bashimov at a recent OSCE conference in Warsaw. A new law adopted in 2024, aligned with UN recommendations and the Palermo Protocol, expands legal guarantees for victims and legally defines potential victims for the first time, aiding timely identification of at-risk individuals.

item.title: UNICEF Provided Health Services to Over 6 Million Afghans in August
item.description: UNICEF announced it delivered essential health services to 6.6 million people across Afghanistan in August. Services were provided through 2,390 fixed and 16 mobile health centers. During the same period, 149,476 people received safe drinking water, and 135,164 gained access to sanitation. Nutrition and health information was given to 433,568 individuals.

item.title: Iran Reports Fourfold Increase in Synthetic Drug Seizures Near Afghanistan Border
item.description: Iranian officials reported a fourfold increase in the seizure of synthetic drugs along the Razavi Khorasan Province border with Afghanistan during the first six months of the current year compared to last year. Officials seized 1.5 tonnes of narcotics, including opium, heroin, and industrial drugs, with crystal methamphetamine being a significant portion.

item.title: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Urges Taliban to Act Against Terrorist Groups
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has called on the Taliban to take concrete, verifiable, and irreversible steps against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and other terrorist groups. Dar stressed that Afghan territory must not be used for terrorist attacks against Pakistan or other countries, accusing India of supporting such groups.

item.title: Poland Deploys 20,000 Police Officers to Schools Amidst Armed Attacks
item.description: Poland has deployed 20,000 police officers to schools following a series of armed attacks. Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced strict measures against the rise of youth violence after three stabbing incidents occurred in educational institutions within four days.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Palestine Discuss Educational Grants for Palestinian Students
item.description: Kazakhstan and Palestine have discussed providing educational grants for Palestinian students to study in Kazakhstan. The meeting between Kazakhstan's Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Isagaliyev and Palestinian Ambassador Montaser Abu Zeid also covered regional and international issues, including the Middle East situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan warns teens about heart risks from chest blows
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office has warned teenagers about the dangers of chest blows, which can cause sudden cardiac arrest even without visible injuries. The office stated that such actions, perceived as jokes or discipline, can lead to tragic outcomes and legal consequences.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes "O'Z" Philosophy for Economic Development and Investment
item.description: President of Uzbekistan introduced the "O'Z" philosophy for the nation's economy, emphasizing Uzbekistan, change, selfhood, and responsibility. He stated that capital and honest labor have no nationality, welcoming all investors contributing to development.

item.title: US Dollar Exchange Rate Rises for Sixth Consecutive Day in Uzbekistan
item.description: The US dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased for the sixth consecutive day. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 13.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency Investigates Allegations of Fraudulent Property Purchases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency (FMA) has investigated claims that a relative of Perizat Kairat purchased apartments in Dubai with money obtained through fraud. The agency stated that the allegation, which spread via an anonymous Telegram channel, was not confirmed. The FMA previously noted Kairat's misuse of charitable funds for personal purchases.

item.title: Yandex Addresses Erroneous Money Deductions for Kazakhstan Users Following Service Disruptions
item.description: Yandex is investigating and addressing erroneous money deductions experienced by users in Kazakhstan following recent service disruptions. The company stated that while many services are gradually being restored, some payment functions may still encounter errors or delays. Yandex assured users that each case of incorrect charges will be reviewed, though support response times may be longer due to increased demand.

item.title: Afghanistan Reports Progress in Preventing Child Marriage Amid UNICEF's Call for Action
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Vice and Virtue reports preventing several cases of forced and underage marriages in the past five months, including attempts to marry girls aged six and eight. UNICEF urges increased investment in girls' education, healthcare, and protection, highlighting child marriage's detrimental effects and advocating for girls' continued access to education.

item.title: Top Global Crypto Funds Invest Billions in Astana Tech Project
item.description: Kazakhstan-based tech project Network School has secured multi-billion dollar investments at a $2 billion business valuation. Major international venture capital and crypto players, including Polychain Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, and Coinbase, are participating. The announcement was made at the Network State Conference 2026.

item.title: Flash Floods Predicted in Tajikistan Over the Next Two Days
item.description: Tajikistan's Hydrometeorological Agency has warned residents of potential flash floods on October 13 and 14. Heavy rainfall is expected to cause floods in mountainous and foothills regions of Sughd, Khatlon, districts of republican subordination, and western Gorno-Badakhshan. Residents are advised to take precautions.

item.title: New Acting Governor Appointed for Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Zaynilobiddin Nizomiddinov has been appointed as the acting governor of Sirdaryo region. He was previously the governor of Bekobod district. A source in the government confirmed his appointment to Daryo.uz. Nizomiddinov has been released from his previous position.

item.title: Man Arrested for Demanding $840,000 for Construction Permits in Bostanliq
item.description: A 56-year-old man has been arrested in Tashkent for allegedly demanding $840,000 to secure permits for constructing residential buildings on 4 hectares of non-residential land in Bostanliq district, Tashkent region. The Interior Ministry reported the man, a construction materials trader, promised to obtain the permits through contacts in the State Cadastre Agency.
